Polar bears, arctic wolves and caribou roam a landscape where hundreds of archaeological sites tell the story of Inuit who have lived and travelled here for thousands of years. Park office: [Complete schedule](https://parks.canada.ca/pn-np/nu/ukkusiksalik/visit/heures-hours) ### \#UkkusiksalikNP - [Facebook](https://www.facebook.com/ParksCanadaNunavut/) - [Twitter](https://x.com/ParksCanNunavut) ## More places to discover with Parks Canada [![](https://pcweb2.azureedge.net/-/media/WET4/proximite-nearby/nu/auyuittuq-640x360.jpg?modified=20221126220409)](https://parks.canada.ca/pn-np/nu/auyuittuq) ### [Auyuittuq National Park](https://parks.canada.ca/pn-np/nu/auyuittuq) Home to spectacular natural landmarks like the Akshayuk Pass, Thor Peak and the Penny Ice Cap, Auyuittuq is the “land that never melts” in Inuktitut. [![](https://pcweb2.azureedge.net/-/media/WET4/proximite-nearby/nu/qausuittuq-640x360.jpg?modified=20221126220409)](https://parks.canada.ca/pn-np/nu/qausuittuq) ### [Qausuittuq National Park](https://parks.canada.ca/pn-np/nu/qausuittuq) A home for the endangered Peary caribou and a traditional Inuit hunting and fishing area on Bathurst Island in Nunavut’s High Arctic. [![](https://pcweb2.azureedge.net/-/media/WET4/proximite-nearby/nu/quttinirpaaq-640x360.jpg?modified=20221126220410)](https://parks.canada.ca/pn-np/nu/quttinirpaaq) ### [Quttinirpaaq National Park](https://parks.canada.ca/pn-np/nu/quttinirpaaq) Inuktitut for “land at the top of the world”, Quttinirpaaq is Canada’s northernmost national park, a vast arctic wilderness on Ellesmere Island. [![](https://pcweb2.azureedge.net/-/media/WET4/proximite-nearby/nu/sirmilik-640x360.jpg?modified=20221126220410)](https://parks.canada.ca/pn-np/nu/sirmilik) ### [Sirmilik National Park](https://parks.canada.ca/pn-np/nu/sirmilik) Narwhals, belugas, polar bears and thousands of seabirds thrive in the Arctic landscape of Bylot Island and Baffin Island’s Borden Peninsula. [![](https://pcweb2.azureedge.net/-/media/WET4/proximite-nearby/nu/epaves-wrecks-640x360.jpg?modified=20221126220409)](https://parks.canada.ca/lhn-nhs/nu/epaveswrecks) ### [Wrecks of HMS Erebus and HMS Terror National Historic Site](https://parks.canada.ca/lhn-nhs/nu/epaveswrecks) Learn about Sir John Franklin’s legendary 1845 expedition and the role of Inuit knowledge in the discoveries of the shipwrecks. # Boating, hiking and wildlife tours

## Ukkusiksalik National Park

Getting to the park by boat with an experienced
outfitter is a great Arctic adventure and a
wonderful way to experience Wager Bay. It is
the safest way to view polar bears and the surest
way to see the abundant marine life including
seals, beluga whales, walrus, orca, bowhead and
occasional narwhal. Kayaking is discouraged
because of the extreme polar bear risk.

From Wager Bay, it is possible to do day hikes
along the coast and rolling hills inland with an
experienced guide or outfitter and Bear Guard.
Viewing opportunities abound for both wildlife
and countless cultural sites scattered throughout
the park. Hike along the Sila River, see the impressive reversing waterfall and visit the remnants of a Hudson’s Bay Company trading post.

Daylight in the summer months will never limit
your hiking options, but tide schedules may since
the swift currents and long tidal flats influence
boat access.

# Polar bear safety

## Ukkusiksalik National Park

### [Avoiding an encounter](https://parks.canada.ca/pn-np/nu/ukkusiksalik/securite-safety/ours-bears/eviter-avoid)

Essential safety tips and how to plan ahead to reduce the risk of encountering polar bears in Ukkusiksalik.

### [Handling an encounter](https://parks.canada.ca/pn-np/nu/ukkusiksalik/securite-safety/ours-bears/rencontre-encounter)

What to do if your group encounters a polar bear in Ukkusiksalik, how to prepare, and how to get help in an emergency.

### [Choosing a safe campsite](https://parks.canada.ca/pn-np/nu/ukkusiksalik/securite-safety/ours-bears/camping)

Where to set up your tent, places to avoid, and best practices to prevent polar bears from approaching your camp in Ukkusiksalik.

### [Deterrents and warning systems](https://parks.canada.ca/pn-np/nu/ukkusiksalik/securite-safety/ours-bears/dispositifs-deterrents)

Bear spray, noisemakers, electric fences and other polar bear deterrents to keep your group safe in Ukkusiksalik.

Polar bears are far more abundant in Ukkusiksalik than in most other Arctic parks. Encounters are likely on any trip. Because of this extreme danger, visitors must travel in the park with a properly equipped and licensed guide who is
experienced in polar bear country.

By choosing to travel in polar bear country you not only accept the associated risks, but also the responsibility to alter your plans, actions and attitudes to accommodate these magnificent animals.

Nanuq, the great white bear, is found in many of Canada’s northern national parks and in some national historic sites. Whenever bears and people occupy the same area, conflict can arise. Polar bears and people have coexisted for thousands of years but contact between the two must be minimized to continue this legacy. Successful polar bear conservation requires your cooperation.

Each encounter with a polar bear is unique. Good judgment, common sense, and familiarity with polar bear behaviour are required in all situations. This information provides guidelines for avoiding and dealing with polar bear encounters. For your safety and the safety of the bears, please read this section carefully and seriously consider the risks involved with travel in polar bear country.

Report polar bear sightings, tracks and signs to Parks Canada staff as soon as possible by radio or satellite phone. If immediate contact is not possible, please record detailed notes for later submission.

For more information, you can speak with our park staff, read the Safety in Polar Bear Country pamphlet  and watch the “Polar Bears: A Guide to Safety” DVD at the park office or distributed at [www.magiclanternmedia.com](https://www.magiclanternmedia.com/catalogue/P51414-014).

# Camping and overnight accommodations

## Ukkusiksalik National Park

Find accommodations in Naujaat, Rankin Inlet, Baker Lake, Coral Harbour and Chesterfield Inlet, and learn about backcountry camping in the park.

### [Backcountry camping](https://parks.canada.ca/pn-np/nu/ukkusiksalik/activ/camping/arriere-pays-backcountry)

Camp under the Northern Lights in spring or the Midnight Sun in summer as you explore Ukkusiksalik’s vast arctic landscape.

### [Nearby accommodations](https://parks.canada.ca/pn-np/nu/ukkusiksalik/activ/camping/loger-stay)

Find a hotel, bed and breakfast or other accommodations in Naujaat, Baker Lake, Chesterfield Inlet, Coral Harbour and Rankin Inlet.
